title: 3. Local Context
use_cases: Use when maintaining narrative consistency between sequential story beats
Configure when managing token consumption limits for long-form generation
Implement when bridging scene transitions to ensure logical character reactions
Use when generating immediate follow-up actions based on a short-term history buffer
content:
This is the immediate narrative flow; what happened in the last 30 seconds.

- The Fix: We use a Sliding Window (or “Narrative Scratchpad”). We pass just the last few beat summaries (e.g., the last 3 beats during the Write Phase) to the model. This gives the AI just enough history to write a smooth transition (“Still reeling from the explosion…”) without wasting tokens on the full text of the previous scene.
- The Problem: Transitions. If Scene 4 ends with an explosion, Scene 5 needs to start with the characters coughing in the smoke. If you simply ask the LLM to “Write Scene 5” in a vacuum, it might have them sipping coffee calmly.
